data.name: Asir
data.gender_notes: Asir is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'asara', which means 'to be heavy, to be strong, to be firm'. In Islamic context, it refers to the one who bears the burdens of life with strength and steadfastness. The name Asir carries the meaning “Strong, Firm” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Asir usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, firm and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that represents inner strength and resilience, as well as a connection to one's ancestors and the natural world.
data.etymology: Asir belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong, Firm.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asir total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_arabic.name: عَصِيرٌ
in_arabic.meaning: مَنْ يَنْزِعُهُ اللَهُ فَقَدْ عَصى اللَهَ
in_arabic.long_meaning: عَصِيرٌ: النَّزِعِ عَنِ الحَقِّ وَالإِعْزازِ لِغَيرِهِ، وَهُوَ مِنَ الأَعضَادِ الرَّبَعِيَّةِ، وَالرَّواحِعُ: الَّتي تُصَدِّعُ الَّذي تُعصِّيهِ، وَيَكَونُ عَصِيرًا لِلَّهِ، مُتَعَلِّقًا بِالأَبَدِ، وَهَذَا الْعِزازُ لِغَيرِهِ يُسَمَّى إِعراضاً وَهُوَ غَيرُ مُسَوَّمٍ، وَمُخالَفَةً وَهِيَ مُسَوَّمَةٌ، وَهَذِهِ الَّتِي تُصَدِّعُ الَّذي تُعصِّيهِ فَهِيَ مُسَوَّمَةٌ بِالرَّبِعَةِ الَّتي تُعصِّي اللَهَ وَتُؤَدِّي غَيرَهُ، وَالَّذي يُضَنِّي عَنِ اللَهِ وَيُؤَدِّي غَيرَهُ فَهُوَ رَبَعَةٌ مُسَوَّمَةٌ، وَهَذِهِ الَّتِي تُصَدِّعُ الَّذي تُعصِّيهِ فَهِيَ مَخالِفَةٌ مُسَوَّمَةٌ، وَالَّذي يُضَنِّي عَنِ اللَهِ وَيُؤَدِّي غَيرَهُ فَهُوَ مُخالِفٌ غَيرُ مُسَوَّمٍ

in_english.name: Asir
in_english.meaning: Whoever is taken away by Allah, he has disobeyed Allah
in_english.long_meaning: Asir: is a term that refers to the one who is taken away by Allah, and has disobeyed Him. It is derived from the Arabic root 'asr', which means 'to take away' or 'to seize'. In Islamic theology, Asir refers to the individual who has been taken away from the obedience of Allah and has chosen to follow other paths. This concept is closely related to the idea of 'Khilafah' or the stewardship of the earth, where humans are accountable to Allah for their actions. The term Asir is also used to describe those who have disobeyed Allah and have been taken away from His guidance. In Islamic tradition, Asir is considered a grave sin, as it involves the rejection of Allah's will and the pursuit of one's own desires.

historical_references.context: Asir was a significant center of trade due to its strategic location along the incense and spice routes. The region was ruled by various dynasties, including the Himyarites and the Aksumites.

historical_references.reference: After the advent of Islam, Asir became a part of the Islamic world, and its major city, Zabid, became an important center of Islamic learning and culture.
